subject: Math
prompt: A sample of a radioactive substance takes 18 years to decay to half its original mass. The function m(t)=400(0.5)18t​ gives the approximate mass of this substance, in grams, that remains t years after a 400-gram sample starts to decay.

choices.A: Approximately 50 grams of the sample remains 54 years after the sample starts to decay.
choices.B: The mass of the sample has decreased by approximately 50 grams 54 years after the sample starts to decay.
choices.C: The mass of the sample has decreased by approximately 54 grams 50 years after the sample starts to decay.
choices.D: Approximately 54 grams of the sample remains 50 years after the sample starts to decay.

explanation: Choice A is correct. It's given that the function $m(t) = 400(0.5)^{\frac{t}{18}}$ gives the approximate mass of this substance, in grams, that remains $t$ years after a $400$-gram sample starts to decay. Since the value of $m(54)$ is the value of $m(t)$ when $t = 54$, it follows that $m(54) = 50$ means that the value of $m(t)$ is $50$ when $t = 54$. Therefore, the best interpretation of $m(54) = 50$ in this context is approximately $50$ grams of the sample remains $54$ years after the sample starts to decay.
